established_findings.statement: Large language models can be used to translate natural-language operator intent into network configuration artifacts in prototype and benchmark settings.
established_findings.evidence_type: peer-reviewed papers / preprints (intent-to-configuration, NFV, PreConfig, GraphSynth)
limitations: Evaluations are primarily on curated datasets or testbeds rather than production deployments
Task scopes and output formats vary across studies, limiting direct comparability
Performance depends on prompt/in-context examples and model tuning

established_findings.statement: Verifier-guided or generate–validate–repair workflows improve configuration correctness relative to naïve LLM generation in IaC and related settings.
established_findings.evidence_type: peer-reviewed / conference papers and preprints (TerraFormer, IaC surveys, PreConfig)
limitations: Most reported gains are on IaC or synthetic corpora; direct NetOps network-wide safety gains in live networks are not demonstrated
Verifier quality and coverage determine improvement magnitude

established_findings.statement: Deterministic network verification and reachability tools exist and are effective at finding configuration errors and reachability violations in offline and deployed settings.
established_findings.evidence_type: tool / systems papers (MEV, Kubernetes reachability verifier, network-spec thesis)
limitations: Scalability and applicability differ by tool and network model (overlay/underlay, Kubernetes vs. IP networks)
Some verifiers require accurate control-plane/state abstractions to be effective

established_findings.statement: Agentic and tool-augmented LLM architectures (ReAct, RAG, multi-agent orchestrations) are actively applied to AIOps/RCA and NetOps tasks; they improve functionality but introduce new failure modes (hallucination, irrelevant tool use) that require procedural or tool constraints.
established_findings.evidence_type: conference papers, vision/implementation papers, and surveys (Flow-of-Action, AIOpsLab, agentic surveys, ARC)
limitations: Most systems are demonstrated in controlled experiments or prototypes
Effectiveness depends strongly on tool design, prompt/workflow constraints, and domain-specific SOPs

established_findings.statement: LLM hallucination and miscalibrated confidence are recognized risks; claim-level calibration and self-verification techniques reduce some classes of errors in evaluation benchmarks.
established_findings.evidence_type: research papers and surveys (claim-level calibration, self-verification, self-detection, V&V survey)
limitations: Calibration/self-verification studies are mostly on QA/reasoning benchmarks; operational NetOps claim verification has domain-specific challenges
Post-hoc calibration does not eliminate all hallucination modes, especially under adversarial or out-of-distribution prompts

established_findings.statement: Human-in-the-loop oversight and staged deployment (e.g., canary/progressive delivery) are widely proposed mitigations, but the literature warns about practical limitations and oversight failure modes.
established_findings.evidence_type: scholar articles and system papers (HITL critique, agentic microservices with progressive delivery, AIOpsLab)
limitations: Empirical evidence of human-review efficacy in NetOps-scale deployments is limited
Human oversight can degrade into a ceremonial approval process under time pressure

unresolved_questions.statement: Do LLM-generated network configurations and agentic NetOps actions maintain safety and availability in production networks at scale?
unresolved_questions.evidence_type: review and prototype studies highlighting gaps between prototypes and production
limitations: Existing studies demonstrate prototypes and testbed results but do not provide production-scale longitudinal failure/effect metrics

unresolved_questions.statement: Are there standardized, action-aware benchmarks that adequately evaluate agentic LLMs performing real NetOps change actions with fidelity to deployment risk?
limitations: Multiple surveys flag benchmark gaps, but concrete community-wide standard benchmarks for action-taking NetOps agents are not established in the supplied records

unresolved_questions.statement: Can runtime formal verifiers be integrated into agentic LLM pipelines to provide tractable, low-latency blocking or correction of unsafe configuration changes?
unresolved_questions.evidence_type: tool papers showing verifier capability (TerraFormer uses verifiers for IaC; MEV for network verification)
limitations: TerraFormer reports verifier-guided training in IaC contexts; explicit closed-loop runtime integration for live NetOps agents is not demonstrated in the supplied records

unresolved_questions.statement: How robust are LLM-based NetOps agents to adversarial or distribution-shifted inputs that mimic operator intent but embed malicious or ambiguous constraints?
limitations: Adversarial evaluations exist for LLMs broadly; NetOps-specific adversarial threat models and empirical studies are limited in the supplied records

candidate_gaps.statement: Need for action-aware, provenance-sensitive benchmarks that evaluate end-to-end agentic NetOps behaviors (generation, verification, staged rollout, rollback, auditability).
limitations: Calls for such benchmarks are present, but concrete benchmark designs and community adoption remain to be developed

candidate_gaps.statement: Integration patterns and APIs for combining claim-level LLM confidence estimates with deterministic network verifiers to prioritize human review and automated blocking are underdeveloped.
candidate_gaps.evidence_type: techniques for claim calibration and verifier tool papers
limitations: Conceptual components exist (calibration, verifiers, verifier-guided training) but integrated architectures and evaluation remain limited in supplied records

candidate_gaps.statement: Scarcity of large-scale, realistic labeled corpora of network configurations and operator intents suitable for pretraining/fine-tuning LLMs for NetOps tasks.
candidate_gaps.evidence_type: PreConfig paper and comprehensive survey noting data limitations
limitations: Some datasets and corpora exist in narrower domains, but community-standard large corpora for diverse NetOps scenarios are not evidenced in the supplied records

candidate_gaps.statement: Empirical studies measuring the real-world efficacy and failure modes of human-in-the-loop oversight for LLM-driven NetOps changes are limited.
limitations: Critical perspectives and prototypes exist, but controlled longitudinal empirical evaluations in operational NetOps settings are not present in the supplied records

excluded_claims: LLM agents are production-ready to autonomously apply network configuration changes in live networks without human oversight.
Deterministic elimination of all LLM hallucinations in NetOps is already solved.
Community-standard, action-aware NetOps benchmarks and large-scale production datasets are already established and validated (beyond prototypes and partial corpora).
Runtime closed-loop integration of formal verifiers that fully guarantees safety of agentic LLM changes in production networks has been demonstrated.
